The statement is false: with (σ−q)(σ+q⁻¹) = 0, C: σ ↦ σ⁻¹ together with q ↦ q⁻¹ is a ring involution, and Tits deformation gives χ^λ(C(β)) = bar(χ^λ(β)) for every λ and n. [re-stamp 2026-11-21, plus a ruling check] Diff read since the 2026-11-15 review: voice edits ('we have' to 'one has') and one 'leptons' replaced by a dash. The earlier finding stands. The statement is false: C (sigma to sigma^-1 with q to q^-1) is a ring involution, and chi^lambda(C(beta)) = bar(chi^lambda(beta)) for every lambda and n, checked over Q(q) on the (2,1) representation of H_3 (35 words, 0 mismatches). The proof's chi^(2,1)(pi^-, q0) ~ +1.892 is wrong; the exact value equals the pi^+ value, about -1.044, and it is a numeric at the calibrated q0 inside a proof. Ruling check (owner-rulings.md, 2026-11-21): the closing paragraphs still call H_2 'the lepton sector' and say leptons are the only level where C = bar. Under the current ruling the electron is sigma_0 sigma_1 sigma_0 in B_3, with Hopf-link closure (the trefoil in B_2 is only the backup), so the electron is not in H_2 and that reading is out of date.

Full read of the rewritten proof. ι (q ↦ q⁻¹, σᵢ ↦ σᵢ⁻¹) preserves σ² = hσ + 1 (σ⁻² = 1 − hσ⁻¹ with h̄ = −h) and the palindromic braid relation; ρ' = bar∘ρ∘ι is K-linear and irreducible; Tits deformation at q = 1 identifies χ' = χ^λ, giving χ^λ(Cβ)(q) = χ^λ(β)(q⁻¹). Each step follows. Independently re-checked with sympy over ℚ(q): both 2×2 matrices satisfy the quadratic and braid relations, P = diag(1, q²) gives P σᵢ⁻¹(q) = σᵢ(q⁻¹) P for both generators, and tr(σ₀σ₁⁻¹) = tr(σ₀⁻¹σ₁) = −(q⁴−q²+1)/q², matching the corrected value. The earlier finding (false statement, wrong +1.892 numeric at q₀) is resolved.
